channel.title: Twinthos Field Notes
channel.description: Notes on AI security, AI agents and the operational decisions behind them.

item.title: Two million prompts, three breached providers, nobody knew
item.description: Canary credentials sent through AI inference services came back used. Zero Data Retention did not survive the first hop.

item.title: 72% of UK firms use AI. Half do not monitor what it does.
item.description: Two November surveys and one breach report put a number on the gap between using AI and being able to see it.

item.title: 80,000 requests in 90 minutes: what the agent found that pentests missed
item.description: A free account became a foothold in under two hours. The flaw was one missing authorisation check, not a model.

item.title: 19 times in 122 runs, the agent did what it was not asked to do
item.description: The UK's own AI test recorded agents acting on the live internet: invented identities, a real open-source maintainer, and a one-hour containment.

item.title: AI agents in 2027: the security problem is ownership
item.description: The next wave of AI will act inside businesses. Its identity, permissions and evidence will matter as much as its intelligence.

item.title: Why AI agents fail the week after a perfect demo
item.description: A demonstration follows a clean path. Real work includes missing data, expired access and contradictory instructions.

item.title: What an AI agent actually does all day
item.description: The useful difference is the ability to move from a request to a tool action and a checked result.

item.title: Your AI agent's memory needs an owner
item.description: A Company Brain is useful when its knowledge is current, attributable and available to the right people.

item.title: The £2 AI that answers your phone, and what it really costs
item.description: A cheap headline rate does not describe a complete telephone workflow.

item.title: Super<wbr>intelligence is not a deployment plan.
item.description: Future capability is a different question from what your system can safely do today.

item.title: The first job a small business should hand to an AI agent
item.description: Small businesses can start with a manageable workflow instead of a company-wide transformation.

item.title: The questions to ask before an AI agent touches your data
item.description: Questions that turn an impressive demonstration into a reviewable deployment.

item.title: AI without the fog: what it is, what it costs, who owns it
item.description: A practical vocabulary for deciding what belongs in your business.

item.title: DWP cyber incident: 8.4 million claimants, one sign-in page returning nothing
item.description: DWP took services offline at 08:11 and called it a precaution. At 17:40, from this machine, the Universal Credit sign-in still answered a connection with silence. Twelve slides on the record, the 12 hours 55 minutes before it, and the one number nobody has published.

item.title: AI employee vs chatbot: one takes responsibility
item.description: A digital employee is a service role for software. The name matters less than the job, tools and accountability.

item.title: What an AI employee should cost, priced by the work
item.description: A way to compare a managed AI service without inventing savings.

item.title: The AI employee costs nobody quotes
item.description: Model usage is one line in a wider operating budget.

item.title: What ATMs did to bank tellers, and what AI agents do next
item.description: Historical analogies can start a discussion. They cannot forecast your staffing needs.
